- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model often overcorrects downward — adjust forecast upward to avoid premature reversal.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in the next few days — reduce forecast by 2–5% to account for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is consolidating, model often fails to capture mean reversion — apply a slight downward bias to reflect potential pullback.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates late-period price increases — add 1–3% buffer to final 5–7 days of forecast to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
